title: Smooth proper compactification of a normal finite-field curve
statement:
Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and let $U_0$ be a normal, geometrically
connected separated scheme of
finite type over $k_0$, pure of dimension one. Then $U_0$ is smooth
over $k_0$, and there are a smooth projective geometrically connected
curve $C_0/k_0$ and a dense open immersion

$$
j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0
$$

whose reduced complement $D_0=(C_0-U_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is finite over
$k_0$. The scheme-theoretic terminology is that of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

proof.text: Normality makes every local ring of $U_0$ an integrally closed domain, and finite type over the field $k_0$ makes $U_0$ noetherian. Its geometrical connectedness implies connectedness; the irreducible components of a normal scheme are disjoint open-and-closed subschemes, so connectedness leaves one component and $U_0$ is integral. The generic local ring is a field. At every closed point, pure dimension one gives a one-dimensional noetherian normal local domain, hence a discrete valuation ring by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]; a DVR is regular because its maximal ideal is principal and its Krull dimension is one. Thus $U_0$ is regular. The regular-perfect-field criterion [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth] applies to the finite-type structure morphism and gives that $U_0$ is smooth over $k_0.

Apply [lem-wf-finite-field-curve-quasi-projective] to obtain a locally closed immersion of the integral $U_0$ into projective space and its scheme-theoretic closure $X_0$; the cited statement gives that $X_0$ is integral and projective and that $U_0$ is dense open in $X_0$. Form the normalization $
u:C_0=X_0^
u	o X_0$ using [def-sc-normalization]. By [lem-sc-normalization-properties](a)--(b), $
u$ is finite and surjective, $C_0$ is proper of the same dimension, and the normalization is an isomorphism over the normal open $U_0$. Hence the induced map $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ is a dense open immersion (the generic point lies in the normal open). Since $X_0	o\operatorname{Spec}(k_0)$ is projective and $
u$ is finite, [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] gives that $C_0	o\operatorname{Spec}(k_0)$ is projective in the affine-base case. Finally, the dimension-one and perfect-field clause (c) of [lem-sc-normalization-properties] gives that $C_0$ is smooth over $k_0$; with its finite-type, separated, dimension-one structure this is the claimed smooth projective curve.

Let $E=C_0\setminus U_0$. It is a proper closed subset of the integral one-dimensional scheme $C_0$, so every irreducible closed subset of $E$ is a point and $E$ has dimension at most zero. Since $C_0$ is of finite type over $k_0$, [lem-sc-dim0-finite] makes the underlying set of $E$ a finite set of closed points. The reduced induced subscheme $D_0=E_{\mathrm{red}}$, defined by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], has the same finite underlying set; each of its residue fields is finite over the finite field $k_0$, so $D_0\to\operatorname{Spec}(k_0)$ is finite. For every field extension $k_1/k_0$, the open $U_{k_1}=U_0\times_{k_0}k_1$ is connected by the hypothesis of geometric connectedness and remains dense in $C_{k_1}=C_0\times_{k_0}k_1$. The closure of a connected subset is connected, so $C_{k_1}$ is connected. Since this holds for every field extension, the definition in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] gives that $C_0$ is geometrically connected.
